mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a month is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat during the same month of the rate hike, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 3.8% for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market tightening supports inflation expectations and equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or the correlation with UNRATE change is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real personal consumption) exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 2%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting stronger demand for equities.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or the signal is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO above its 12-month moving average of at least 5% predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as contraction in industrial production suggests weakening economic momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or the effect is not robust across multiple contraction episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL by more than 0.25 percentage points each over a 3-month window are associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return, reflecting dual inflation and policy accommodation.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL each rise >0.25% monthly for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: Dual inflation and rate hike cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or the interaction is not statistically significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS below 150,000 in a month coincides with a negative S&P 60-day forward return as elevated joblessness signals recession risk and investor caution.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or the signal fails to predict direction in multiple prior recessions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (household spending) rises by more than 4% from the prior month, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating strong consumer demand supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive or the signal is spurious (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime where RSAFS (retail sales) falls for three consecutive months below its 6-month moving average is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak retail activity signals economic softness.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < RSAFS[6m] for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the effect is not robust across multiple such episodes (p > 0.05).
